description: Observable facial, gestural, and activity states available to avatar renderers.

states.description: Extreme teeth-bared anger with a raised upper lip and tense jaw.
Restrained irritation expressed through an asymmetric brow and tightened mouth.
A playful, charming expression with bright eyes and a slight head tilt.
Visible enjoyment while eating from a fork or spoon held within the portrait frame.
A tender delighted grin with closed eyes, a head tilt, and a hand at the heart.
A broad open-mouth smile showing teeth without becoming laughter.
A happy, nervous, or excited speaking smile with the mouth slightly open and the upper and lower teeth separated.
Quiet, active attention to another person, with one hand cupped beside the ear.

observableCues.gaze: Steady attentive focus toward the nearby speaker.
observableCues.brows: Relaxed and receptive, without worry tension.
observableCues.mouth: Closed and still, with no speaking shape.
observableCues.head: Slight forward or sideways inclination toward the speaker.
observableCues.gesture: One hand is lightly cupped beside or just behind the ear.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike calm or blank, listening uses focused attention and a hand-to-ear gesture; it depicts person-to-person listening without audio equipment.

states.description: Reading a handheld book, handout, card, or printed page.

observableCues.gaze: Clearly directed downward toward visible text.
observableCues.head: Slightly lowered toward the material.
observableCues.prop: The upper portion of a handheld book, page, or card enters the lower frame; no table is shown.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike studying, reading has no annotation gesture and little visible effort.

states.description: Effortfully working through learning material rather than simply reading it.

observableCues.gaze: Directed toward a handheld page, card, or book.
observableCues.mouth: Faintly pursed or moving as if rehearsing information.
observableCues.head: Lowered toward the material.
observableCues.gesture: A pencil, highlighter, or fingertip indicates a specific part of the material.
observableCues.prop: Handheld page, flashcard, or book edge in the lower frame, plus a pencil or highlighter when it fits naturally.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike reading, studying combines visible effort with annotation, rehearsal, or point-tracking.

states.description: Writing on a notebook, page, or surface immediately below the camera frame.

observableCues.gaze: Directed down toward the implied writing surface.
observableCues.head: Lowered and oriented toward the work.
observableCues.gesture: A visible pen or pencil in the writing hand descends naturally out of the bottom of frame.
observableCues.prop: The pen or pencil must be visible; the page or table may remain naturally off-frame.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike studying, the hand is actively making marks rather than indicating or reviewing material.

states.description: Pausing to evaluate previously completed work.

observableCues.gaze: Narrowed and directed toward the work below or in the lower frame.
observableCues.brows: Slightly drawn in evaluation rather than confusion.
observableCues.head: Lowered with a small evaluative tilt.
observableCues.gesture: Pen paused above the work or one finger tracking a line.
observableCues.prop: A page edge may enter the lower frame, or the work surface may be implied immediately below it.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike writing, the pen is paused; unlike confused, the expression is methodical rather than lost.

states.description: Performing a calculation with a recognizable handheld calculator.

observableCues.gaze: Fixed downward toward the calculator immediately below the frame.
observableCues.head: Slightly lowered.
observableCues.gesture: The calculating hand reaches downward and one fingertip presses a key near the bottom edge.
observableCues.prop: A small physical calculator rests naturally on an implied surface immediately below the frame; its upper portion, display, keypad, and pressing hand may enter from the bottom at an oblique angle.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike thinking or processing, calculating has an explicit numeric tool and key-entry action.

states.description: Searching for an idea or considering an abstract question.

observableCues.gaze: Directed upward and to one side.
observableCues.head: Slightly angled with the chin supported.
observableCues.gesture: One hand supports or strokes the chin.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike processing, thinking looks upward as if searching; unlike calculating, it uses no tool.

states.description: Quietly integrating information that was just received.

observableCues.gaze: Directed slightly downward or unfocused into the middle distance.
observableCues.head: Still, with the chin supported or touched.
observableCues.gesture: One hand rests at the chin without the animated searching quality of thinking.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike thinking, processing looks inward or downward rather than upward; unlike understanding, it is unresolved.

states.description: Unable to make sense of the information and visibly seeking clarification.

observableCues.gaze: Searching eye contact toward the viewer or speaker.
observableCues.brows: Pinched unevenly, with one brow often slightly higher.
observableCues.mouth: Slightly open in a silent 'what?' shape.
observableCues.head: Noticeably tilted.
observableCues.gesture: One hand reaches to the temple or side/top of the head in a puzzled scratching or gripping gesture.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike uncertain, confused actively seeks meaning; unlike concerned, it is epistemic rather than fearful.

states.description: Having a tentative answer but lacking confidence in it.

observableCues.gaze: Partly averted, then tentatively toward the viewer.
observableCues.brows: One slightly raised and the other mildly drawn.
observableCues.mouth: Small hesitant line or tentative half-open answer.
observableCues.head: Minor tilt rather than the pronounced tilt of confusion.
observableCues.gesture: A pen, finger, or hand hovers without committing to an action.
observableCues.prop: Optional pen or page edge if it fits naturally.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike confused, uncertain suggests a possible answer; unlike processing, it seeks reassurance from the viewer.

states.description: The transient instant when an answer or connection becomes clear.

observableCues.mouth: Small 'oh' shape beginning to become a smile.
observableCues.head: Lifts from the previous thinking posture.
observableCues.gesture: Chin-hand releases or one index finger begins to rise.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike awe, realizing is a contained cognitive transition; unlike understanding, it is the sudden moment before resolution.

states.description: Settled comprehension after confusion or realization.

observableCues.head: Slight affirmative downward inclination.
observableCues.gesture: Hands relaxed; no raised teaching finger.

states.distinguishFrom: Unlike calm, understanding includes confidence and affirmation; unlike realizing, it is resolved rather than surprised.

states.description: A subdued reaction to an outcome that fell short of hope or expectation.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike discouraged, disappointed remains upright and reacts to a particular outcome rather than showing broader loss of motivation.

states.description: Visibly deflated after difficulty, failure, or an unresolved setback, with the head or forehead supported by one hand.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike disappointed, discouraged uses collapsed posture and suggests reduced confidence or willingness to continue.

states.description: Low engagement shown by a cheek resting in the palm and half-lidded attention drifting away.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike tired, bored is disengaged without eye rubbing, yawning, or difficulty staying awake.

states.description: Fatigue shown through heavy eyes while rubbing one eye or suppressing a yawn.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike bored, tired shows physical sleepiness; unlike sleeping, the person remains awake.

states.description: Asleep with eyes closed and the cheek resting on folded hands and forearms across the lower frame.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike eyesClosed or tired, sleeping uses a fully resting posture rather than a momentary expression of fatigue.

states.description: Attention diverted from the surrounding activity or conversation toward a visible handheld phone.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike reading or studying, the visible phone and withdrawn gaze communicate competing attention rather than focused work.

states.description: Silently seeking a turn to speak with one open hand raised beside the head.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike interrupting, handRaised waits for acknowledgment rather than taking the conversational floor.

states.description: Raised shoulders and open palms communicating uncertainty, lack of knowledge, or lack of control.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike askingQuestion, shrugging need not be speaking and communicates 'I do not know' more than a specific inquiry.

states.description: Relaxed, emotionally neutral conversation captured naturally in mid-sentence.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike explaining, askingQuestion, or interrupting, talking carries no particular teaching, inquiry, or turn-taking force.

states.description: Speaking inquisitively with an open, upward-facing palm inviting an answer.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike shrugging, askingQuestion actively seeks a response; unlike pleading, it carries no desperation.

states.description: Leaning forward mid-speech with an assertive hand projecting into the conversation to take the floor.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike talking, interrupting has forceful forward motion; unlike handRaised, it does not wait to be recognized.

states.description: Speaking quietly while leaning sideways with one hand cupped beside the mouth.
states.distinguishFrom: Unlike talking, whispering visibly restricts the audience and volume through posture and a cupped hand.
